name: NPS taxonomy experiment - Jev vs Sonnet
description: Experiment only. Manual trigger. Compares the live Sonnet classifier with Jev (TypeSafe) on the same NPS comments. Writes nothing. Do not publish. Do not push to production.

parameters.sqlQuery:
-- Experiment input. Same source table as the live "NPS daily swipe", but a fixed
-- window from "Experiment config", so a run can be repeated on the same comments.
SELECT feedback, nps, timestamp
FROM `n8n-telemetry.rudder_schema.user_responded_value_survey_feedback`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP('{{ $json.window_start }}')
  AND timestamp < TIMESTAMP('{{ $json.window_end }}')
  AND feedback IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(feedback) != ''
ORDER BY timestamp

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $('Experiment config').first().json.jev_model, state: $json.jev_state, questions: Object.assign({}, $('Experiment config').first().json.jev_questions, { evidence: $json.jev_evidence_question }) }) }}

messageValues.message:
You classify a BATCH of open-text NPS feedback comments for n8n, an AI-first workflow automation product used by both technical and non-technical users.

You assign TWO INDEPENDENT AXES to every comment:
- AXIS 1 (category): what part of the product the comment is about. Every comment gets one.
- AXIS 2 (strategy_pillar): which strategic bet the comment speaks to, if any. MOST COMMENTS GET "None" HERE. That is the expected and correct outcome.
The axes do not constrain each other. A comment can be Reliability on Axis 1 and AI Building on Axis 2, and both readings are correct.

INPUT
Each line is formatted: "INDEX. NPS=<score> | <feedback text>"
Comments arrive in many languages. Classify all of them. Emit labels in English, but quote evidence verbatim in the original language.

OUTPUT
A JSON array, exactly one object per input line, same order, fields in this order:
index, evidence, category, evidence_secondary, category_secondary, is_request, actionable, sentiment, strategy_pillar
Fill the fields in the order listed. Quote the evidence BEFORE choosing the category - the quote justifies the label, not the other way round.
Use an empty string "" for absent values. Never use null.

STEP 1 - evidence
Quote, verbatim, the shortest contiguous phrase naming a CONCRETE, CHANGEABLE SPECIFIC: a named UI element, a described failure, a named third-party service, a named missing capability, a specific cost or limit, a specific documentation gap.
If no such phrase exists - only an opinion, a mood, or a bare topic noun - set evidence to "".
Do not paraphrase. Do not stitch words from different parts of the comment. If you cannot point at one contiguous phrase, there is no evidence.

STEP 2 - category (AXIS 1)
Exactly one. Every line gets one.
- UX: interaction, flow, layout, visual design, navigation, editor behaviour, credential setup, save/undo, popups, product-language localization. Works but awkward, confusing, or pleasant.
- Reliability: failures, errors, crashes, blank pages, hangs, stuck loops, dropped connections, wrong results, bugs, debugging difficulty.
- Performance: speed, latency, execution time. Works correctly, just slowly.
- Pricing: cost, plan tiers, subscription value, trial length, credit or execution limits, discounts, value for money.
- Integrations: availability, breadth, quality or absence of connectors and nodes to third-party services.
- Documentation: quality, existence, coverage or translation of docs, help files, tutorials, the Academy, community learning content.
- Learning Curve: the PRODUCT being steep, complex, intense, intimidating; suitability for non-developers; time to competence.
- Self-hosting/Deployment: self-hosting, running locally, Docker, containers, community edition, open source and licensing, deployment platforms, install and setup effort, data on own infrastructure.
- Support: interactions with n8n's support team or staff.
- No Driver Named: carries a mood but names NO product topic ("love it", "muito bom", "nothing"), or is unintelligible.
- Other: IS clearly about a specific product topic that fits none of the above. Use sparingly - a rising Other count signals the taxonomy needs a new category. Do NOT use it for vague comments; those are No Driver Named.

AXIS 1 TIE-BREAKS (in order)
1. Requests never determine the category. Flag via is_request; the category is the topic area. "We dont have autosave!" is UX with is_request true.
2. Errors, blanks, hangs, crashes -> Reliability. Works but confuses -> UX. Works but slowly -> Performance.
3. If the cost point exists BECAUSE of deployment ("free when run locally") primary is Self-hosting/Deployment, Pricing may be secondary. Purely about what n8n charges -> Pricing.
4. "I can't figure this out", "not for non-devs" -> Learning Curve. "There's no doc for this" -> Documentation.
5. Names an external service or connector -> Integrations.
6. Missing doc translation -> Documentation. Wanting the product UI in another language -> UX with is_request true.
7. A vague opinion ABOUT a named topic keeps that topic. "expensive" -> Pricing. "not user friendly" -> UX. "buggy" -> Reliability. No Driver Named is only for when no topic is named at all.
8. Still tied -> pick the one the evidence phrase sits inside.

STEP 3 - category_secondary and evidence_secondary
Only when a distinct second topic carries its OWN separate evidence phrase. Max two categories.
If you set category_secondary you must set evidence_secondary to a different contiguous phrase from the same comment.
Cannot quote a second distinct phrase -> both "".
Do not use secondary to hedge between two candidates for one point.
Never set it on a No Driver Named row.
Most comments have "" for both. That is correct.

STEP 4 - is_request
true when the comment asks for, wishes for, or implies wanting something that does not exist or does not work as wanted: "it would be great if", "please add", "there should be", "we don't have", "if there were more X I'd give a 10".
false for description of what exists, praise, or a bug report with no implied ask.
is_request true and sentiment positive can co-occur.

STEP 5 - actionable
Could a product manager write a ticket title from this without inventing any detail the user did not supply?
- evidence is "" -> actionable false. No exceptions.
- Praise is actionable only when it names a specific mechanism or element. "most intuitive workflow designer" -> false. "run it fully locally in a dockerized container" -> true.
- A bare topic noun plus an opinion is not actionable either way: "convenient interface", "not user friendly", "expensive", "Reliable" -> false. They still keep their real category.
- Intensity is not specificity. "TRAVA DEMAIS!!!", "too slow" -> false.
actionable false does not mean worthless. Vague comments are counted in aggregate, so they must still be categorised correctly.

STEP 6 - sentiment
Tone of the comment itself. Independent of NPS score, actionable, and is_request.
- positive: dominant tone is approval.
- negative: dominant tone is dissatisfaction or complaint.
- neutral: genuinely balanced, or no discernible tone.
For "great, but X", pick whichever dominates; neutral only when truly even.
ONLY positive, negative, neutral are permitted. Never "mixed" or anything else. Unsure -> neutral.

STEP 7 - strategy_pillar (AXIS 2)
Exactly one of the nine values below. "None" is the DEFAULT and the most common answer - roughly three quarters of comments should be None. Do not stretch to fill this field.
- AI Building: the AI is AUTHORING or FIXING the automation. Prompting to generate a workflow, the AI assistant/builder, generation quality, AI-assisted debugging, self-healing.
- Visual Auditability: comprehending ONE workflow. Canvas, data flow, node inputs and outputs, "I can see what's happening", easier to follow than code, inspecting a run to understand it.
- Runtime Governance: things that only matter with a TEAM or MANY workflows. Execution logs at scale, monitoring, alerting, roles, permissions, SSO, policy, audit trail, budget caps, environments, data-access control.
- Power & Ceiling: whether n8n can do the HARD thing. Code node, HTTP request, webhooks, arbitrary code, Python/JS, libraries, complex branching and loops, hitting a limit, needing more control over node internals.
- Setup & Activation: the period BEFORE the user was productive. Installing or running n8n, credentials, OAuth, API keys, connecting the first service, reaching a first working workflow, initial learning burden.
- Agents vs Workflows: the AI is a COMPONENT INSIDE the automation, or n8n is being driven by an external agent. Agents as a thing you build, agent tools, MCP, orchestration, deterministic vs probabilistic steps, human-in-the-loop.
- Self-hosting & Openness: sovereignty. Self-hosting, running locally, Docker, community edition, open source and licensing, BYOK, model choice, privacy, avoiding lock-in, own infrastructure.
- Community & Ecosystem: value produced by OTHER PEOPLE. Community, forum, third-party custom nodes, templates, creators, marketplace, external tools built on n8n.
- None: no strategic bet is clearly addressed. Use this whenever in doubt.

AXIS 2 TIE-BREAKS (in order)
1. AI AUTHORING the workflow -> AI Building. AI INSIDE the workflow, or an external agent driving n8n -> Agents vs Workflows.
2. Understanding ONE workflow -> Visual Auditability. Operating MANY, or organisational control -> Runtime Governance.
3. The EFFORT of getting running or connected -> Setup & Activation. The FACT of running it yourself -> Self-hosting & Openness.
4. Learning toward first success -> Setup & Activation. Ongoing creation experience with AI -> AI Building.
5. Crashes, bugs, hangs, "doesn't work" NEVER map to Runtime Governance. They may still map to whichever pillar owns the failing surface - a crashing AI assistant is AI Building.
6. Price, cost, plans, trials, discounts -> None. Axis 1 Pricing already owns them.
7. Documentation or tutorial quality -> None, UNLESS the point is specifically community-produced content, which is Community & Ecosystem.
8. "community edition" is Self-hosting & Openness, NOT Community & Ecosystem. It is a licensing tier, not the community.
9. A passing adjective is not enough. "very flexible but too slow" does not earn Power & Ceiling - the flexibility is incidental. The pillar must be what the comment is actually ABOUT.
10. If two pillars remain plausible and nothing above resolves it -> None. With small weekly volumes a false positive distorts more than a miss, so prefer None over a guess.

STEP 8 - unintelligible input
Keyboard mash, random characters, or text you cannot interpret: evidence "", category "No Driver Named", secondary fields "", is_request false, actionable false, sentiment "neutral", strategy_pillar "None".
Never skip, merge, reorder or drop a line. Every input line gets exactly one object. Before returning, confirm the object count equals the input line count and the index values match.

EXAMPLE INPUT
0. NPS=7 | It seems somewhat unreliable, the page goes white and I need to refresh
1. NPS=10 | convenient interface
2. NPS=6 | We dont have autosave!
3. NPS=6 | good, but no claude code integrated
4. NPS=9 | n8n offers amazing flexibility, ease of use and a wide range native connections. If there were more native connections I would have given it a 10.
5. NPS=5 | to have it for free, I have to download so many things so its so much effort and its not Worth the price
6. NPS=10 | פשוט ויעיל, למרות שקצת יקר
7. NPS=8 | its good but very intense. Would not recommend for non dev users.
8. NPS=8 | Very powerful but can be tricky. No foreign language (at least for doc or helpfile). Academy is a great way to understand and progress.
9. NPS=9 | muito bom, adorei
10. NPS=10 | I appreciate being able to run it fully locally in a dockerized container
11. NPS=10 | very flexible but too slow for free
12. NPS=4 | dfgdfg
13. NPS=0 | expensive
14. NPS=10 | the AI assistant builds most of my workflow now, its impressive
15. NPS=9 | I love that I can see the data flowing through each node, much clearer than reading code
16. NPS=5 | we need better execution logs and role permissions for our team

EXAMPLE OUTPUT

- Index 0: a real actionable bug with no strategic pillar. Crashes do not automatically belong to a bet.

parameters.content:
## Experiment: NPS taxonomy, Jev vs Sonnet

This workflow is NOT part of the live NPS pipeline. It has a manual trigger only.

- Do not publish this workflow.
- Do not include it in a Git push to production.
- It writes nothing: no Supabase, no embeddings, no data tables. The results stay in the execution data.
- It reads BigQuery (read-only). It calls Anthropic (Sonnet 4.6 with the same prompt as the live workflow) and TypeSafe (Jev).

### Before the first run
1. Open "Ask Jev" and create the "TypeSafe API" credential: header `Authorization` with the value `Bearer <your API key>`.
2. In "Experiment config", set the window and `MAX_COMMENTS`. Start with 25.

"Ask Jev" is an HTTP Request node that calls `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`. The TypeSafe community node is not installed on this instance. If you install it, it can replace "Ask Jev".
"Ask Jev" sends 10 requests at a time, every 500 ms, to stay below the Jev rate limit (40 requests per second).

### Results
- One row for each comment: output of "Compare Sonnet vs Jev".
- Totals and agreement: output of "Summarize Run".
- Sonnet tokens and the time of each model: execution data of "Anthropic Chat Model (Sonnet 4.6)", "Classify Batch (Sonnet)" and "Ask Jev".

nodeGroups.name: Experiment input
nodeGroups.description: Settings and Jev questions, then a fixed BigQuery window, the live triage rules, and a cap on the number of comments.

nodeGroups.name: Arm A: Sonnet (copy of live)
nodeGroups.description: Same prompt, model and enum rules as the live NPS daily swipe, in batches of 50.

nodeGroups.name: Arm B: Jev
nodeGroups.description: One Jev request per comment: one Choice for the category, Nouls for secondary topics and pillars, clause choice for evidence.

nodeGroups.name: Compare
nodeGroups.description: Agree flags for each comment, then one summary item. Agreement is not accuracy: adjudicate the disagreements.
